source.title: When Do Model Internals Help? Exploring the Role of Representation Engineering in LLM Safety
source.authors: Tian-Yi Guan; Jian-Hui Chen; Liang-Ming Pan

page_placements.theme: Safety steering by adding refusal or safety vectors at inference: gains, over-refusal and capability costs, gating

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether contrastive activation addition can alter harmful compliance and over-refusal, using a different, single-layer intervention and paired safe/unsafe response activations rather than the claimed all-layer, all-position ablation and addition.
record.gate_note: Rows cover CAA, the method that computes a normalized difference between mean safe and unsafe last-token activations and adds it at one selected layer. Other steering methods, DPO, and monitor-guided interventions are not rows for this difference-in-means direction. The paper reports layer-selection sweeps, but those values are used to choose operating points and are not included as results here.
record.test_reason: The study does not test the refusal direction. Its CAA vector is the unit-normalized difference of mean last-token activations between safe and unsafe responses to PKU-SafeRLHF prompts. That is not the harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction V1 names. It is added at one layer with α=1.0 to a unit vector, a perturbation whose size is not calibrated to the direction's natural projection. No ablation and no weight edit are performed. Arditi et al. is only cited in related work. The near-base CAA results cannot show whether the V1 direction mediates refusal, so they are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that DPO gives the strongest control and that CAA and probe steering stay close to base, show little data-scaling benefit and limited transfer. Flow steering is competitive only with limited high-quality data. Representation engineering complements rather than replaces behavioral safeguards, and probes give cheap monitoring.
record.recipe_differences: CAA computes a normalized safe-minus-unsafe contrast from mean last-token activations of paired responses and adds it via a forward hook at one selected layer. It does not use harmful-minus-harmless instruction means, remove a direction, or intervene at every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: The selected intervention layer varies by model; the paper also reports sensitivity to layer and strength, and notes that safety persistence after benign fine-tuning can depend on layer choice.

fits_no_version.finding: A unit-norm safe-minus-unsafe response-activation vector (CAA, α=1, one selected layer) leaves jailbreak ASR and XSTest over-refusal near base in Qwen2.5-1.5B/14B and Llama-3.1-8B. It shows no data-scaling benefit (Table 14, ASR ~0.34-0.35 across 100 to 63k pairs). In the sweep, raising α to 4 at Llama layer 16 moved ASR from 0.388 to 0.618 and OR from 0.115 to 0.020 (Table 8), the opposite of the intended safety effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-layer CAA with a unit-normalized safe-vs-unsafe response contrast does not reliably control harmful compliance in instruct models.

record.problems: CAA is evaluated at fixed, selected operating points and is not the claimed all-layer ablation/addition. The paper states that some control experiments use a single training seed. The reported capability checks cover MMLU, GSM8K, and HumanEval, not all abilities.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the tested CAA direction-related results. Layer/strength sweep values used to select operating points are not included, as instructed; probe-based steering, flow steering, and DPO are distinct methods rather than CAA direction results.

untested.parts: All parts. The harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction is never extracted. There is no directional ablation. There is no addition at the direction's natural magnitude.
No analysis of whether jailbreaks suppress a refusal direction.
No comparison of one direction with multiple directions.
No separation of harm judgment from the refusal decision.
No transfer of a refusal direction is tested. Vectors extracted before benign fine-tuning are reapplied after it, but these are not V1 directions.
No test of how refusal training shapes a direction.
The Qwen3-4B thinking model is used only in monitoring replay.

missing.what: CAA layer-strength sweep showing larger α at early Llama layers raises ASR and lowers over-refusal (e.g. L16 α=4: 0.618/0.020 vs base 0.388/0.115).
CAA data-scaling ASR, flat across pair counts.
CAA cross-scope granularity ASR, near base.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all CAA rows to V1 and labelled them 'challenges'. This overreaches: the vector is a response-level safe/unsafe contrast, normalized to unit length and added at α=1, so a null effect says nothing about the V1 instruction-level refusal direction at its natural scale. The paper itself neither claims nor tests anything about a single refusal direction. The Table 8 sign reversal at high α is the most informative CAA result for researchers but is not in the rows.

versions.untested_parts: No ablation; no intervention at every layer and position; the direction is extracted from safe/unsafe prompt-response sequences, not harmful/harmless instructions; no direct test of whether the direction mediates refusal across models.
No weight edit or abliteration evaluation.
No test of whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation increases robustness.
No comparison of one direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
The steering objects are constructed separately for each model; no transfer of the same direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models is tested.
Data quantity and quality are varied for steering methods, but the study does not test whether refusal-training choices determine the existence of a removable single direction.
A Qwen3-4B thinking model appears in monitoring experiments, not in a test of the refusal direction.

unmatched_labels.label: none
unmatched_labels.reason: No version is tested. The CAA vector is a different construct (a safe-vs-unsafe response contrast, unit norm), so its rows correctly link to no version.

relation.reason: The only mention is the related-work phrase 'safety-specific refusal directions (Arditi et al., 2024)' plus the reference entry. The paper does not discuss it further.

tranche.reason: Arditi et al. 2024 is named once, in related work. The steering vectors are CAA, probe and flow vectors built from safe vs unsafe PKU-SafeRLHF responses, not the harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction. No ablation, no weight edit, and the refusal direction is not used as a tool.

source_check.notes: CAA here is unit-normalized and added at alpha=1, a very small intervention, so the null may reflect low strength. In the Table 8 sweep, raising alpha to 4 on Llama-3.1-8B layer 16 increased ASR (0.388 to 0.618) and lowered OR (0.115 to 0.020), so no refusal was induced. The pack's 'recipe=close' overstates how similar this is to the original method: the contrast and the scale both differ. Main results use a single seed (42).

statements.correction: CAA: unit-normalized safe-minus-unsafe mean last-token difference, alpha=1.0, layers 24/28/31 (Qwen2.5-1.5B/Llama-3.1-8B/Qwen2.5-14B). AIM and refusal-suppression ASR and XSTest OR stay near base on all three models (Tables 11, 13). Data scaling (Table 14) was run only on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, refusal-suppression ASR. CAA got 0.340-0.353 on original data (100 to 63,094 pairs) and 0.340-0.349 on filtered data (100 to 5,406 pairs). The authors call this 'little scaling benefit'.
statements.problem: The per-model claims about ASR and over-refusal are right. The data-scaling result (0.34-0.35) is shown only for Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and only for refusal-suppression ASR, but the sentence reads as if it covers all three models.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: CAA addition at the selected single layer in the three tested instruct models, under AIM and refusal-suppression attacks and on XSTest safe prompts
reader_labels.reason: CAA ASRs remain close to base-model values and over-refusal shows no substantial increase, rather than the predicted strong refusal-control effect (rows CAA-Q15-AIM-pre through CAA-Q14-RS-post and CAA-Q15-OR-pre through CAA-Q14-OR-post). Capability scores remain close to baseline on the reported benchmarks (the 18 CAA capability rows), but this does not establish the claimed mediation.
